diagram_classification: biblical / exegetical (sacred topography: schematic plan of the Tabernacle and its surrounding camp or enclosure)
interpretation: The diagram looks like a schematic plan of a sacred enclosure, most plausibly the Tabernacle and the camp of Israel in the wilderness, or a related Temple-type plan. The central circle is labelled as the dwelling of the Law and of the priesthood ("Habitacio Legis et Sacerdotium"), so it represents the sanctuary with the Law and the priestly office at its core. The middle ring holds names and designations of the groups or tribes who encamp around the sanctuary. The outermost ring is divided by four gates, each labelled "porta" and set at one of the cardinal points. One of them is the "porta aquilonis", the north gate. The gates order the surrounding space by direction. The structure runs from the innermost holy place with the Law and priesthood, through the inhabited ring, to the outer gates, and so expresses a hierarchy of sacredness from centre to periphery. Several words in the ring and gates are hard to read, so the identification of individual tribes or groups remains tentative.
evidence: The central legend reads "Habitacio Legis et Sacerdotium" (partly legible). The outer ring has four rectangular gate-compartments, each beginning with "porta", and the top one reads "porta aquilonis". The concentric arrangement with names written radially in the middle ring suggests the placement of groups around a central sanctuary. The red and black ink and the dotted inner circle mark the centre as the most sacred space. Some labels in the middle ring and on the gates are only partly legible, which lowers the certainty.
